evidence.text: Demand exiting Q2 was 2,997 bottles in June, against 8,294 for the whole quarter, which means April and May together were 5,297 (about 2,650 a month). Three paths for Q3: June held flat gives about 8,990 bottles and about $6.6M, below the $7.1M bar; the Q2 slope of about +6% a month gives about 10,100 bottles and about $7.4M, about 4% above the bar; the bar itself needs about 9,700 bottles at Q2 pricing. Management said momentum continued into Q3.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-08-13 amc): revenue $6.09M against a $4.3-5.8M consensus, +71% q/q, and the stock moved +2.4% (8.63 to 8.84). Recent beats have bought only small moves.
evidence.why_not_priced: The Street models +16% q/q after a +71% quarter (Earnings Whispers preview). If consensus had extrapolated the June exit rate and the Q2 monthly slope, the bar would sit near $7.4M rather than $7.1M. Revenue per bottle moved from $585 to $734 in one quarter and receivables rose $1.24M in H1. A partial reversal of that pricing would erase the beat, which is why the size is small.
evidence.independence: The Q2 call commentary (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/13/alpha-cognition-acog-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/) says July scripts were strong, Q2 had no material stocking and gross-to-net should stay stable through year-end. evidence.text: Payer access has not moved, as far as anyone has said. The Q2 release says the contracted Part D book was 'consistent at approximately 16%' for a second quarter, with 'expansion expected to accelerate in 2H 2026'. evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no clean prior event. The access shortfall was disclosed in the August print and the stock still rose +2.4%. Since then the stock has drifted -8.7%, and Earnings Whispers ties that partly to the payer question.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is down 8.7% since the last report and the preview names payers as the test. But management's guide of '2H acceleration' is still the official stance, and a third quarter at about 16% would breach it. If the market had fully priced a miss here, the stock would sit near its post-earnings low of $7.98 rather than $8.77. The size is left small because the call could just as easily announce a 2027 contract win, which would be upside.
evidence.independence: The Earnings Whispers preview of 2026-11-05 (https://finviz.com/news/417314/alpha-cognitions-zunvale-ramp-faces-a-payer-test-as-street-models-slower-growth) independently flags that another flat quarter would be a credibility problem. Bottles growing +37% q/q corroborate that ramp, so a raise funds visible demand rather than distress, and the sign is close to zero. What remains is the mechanical risk: a small-cap that raises the morning after a good print usually falls overnight. The probability of that inside this window is low.

evidence.text: The Brazilian real weakened to about 5.45-5.50 per dollar in early November 2026, after Lula's re-election and the BCB's Selic hold at 13.75%. In a deal-pinned stock a miss cuts both ways: it weakens the holdouts' case and makes the tender more likely to succeed (up), and it lowers the standalone value if the deal fails (down). Net near zero, slightly negative.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 revenue $94.1m (+12.7% y/y) moved +2.16 on 2026-05-12, and Q2 2026 revenue $94.3m (+11.2% y/y) moved -0.97 on 2026-08-11. Both came under a non-binding proposal, not a signed tender. There is no history of a revenue miss under a signed deal.

evidence.text: Completion is not assured, and the print plus the call are the first public data a holdout can use. There is also a non-waivable majority-of-the-minority condition, and no tender or support agreements exist. Four Tree Island Advisory (a self-described top-10/15 holder) has argued DDI is worth at least $26.40/ADS, and Stonehill (about 1.0m ADSs) opposed the earlier proposal. Kroll's preliminary ranges ran to $20-25 on consensus estimates and trading multiples. A strong Q3 would arm holdouts and widen the spread; a weak one would do the opposite.

evidence.why_not_priced: A 3.4% spread with 29 days to expiry annualises to about 40%. That is wide for a no-financing-condition deal by a controlling holder, so completion risk is partly priced already. What is not priced is any new holdout statement against $16.25: none was found after 2026-11-09. If one lands with the print it would show as a widening spread.
